馬天そば.name: Batten Soba
馬天そば.desc: A hideaway soba shop quietly tucked into a riverside building, with a distinctive entrance. The No. 1 favorite is the mix soba, loaded with chunks of braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs. Meltingly tender, sweetish meat and a pork-bone-forward blended broth give it a homey feel.
t: * This article was created by Claude Sonnet 4 AI and partly supplemented by me.
I ate here in December 2024 😄 On the way home from our usual weekend post-surf trip, wanting New Year's Eve soba, I went to "Batten Soba" in Sashiki Shinkai, Nanjo City!
Batten Soba
Batten Soba (the entrance is distinctive (^0^;))

Actually, when I ate at Tebichi no Tesuke last time, I spotted this shop's sign and had been curious ever since. This time I went to eat the "Mix Soba," recommended as the No. 1 favorite at "Batten Soba" in Sashiki Shinkai, Nanjo City, which I found when I ate at Tebichi no Tesuke the other day 😆

First, the location of this shop is quite interesting. It quietly sits on the first floor of a white building along a river, but the entrance is a bit unusual, and it's hard to find unless you're a local 😅

From the outside you'd think "Huh, is this a shop?" It gave the impression of a true hidden-gem Okinawa soba shop known only to those in the know. If the red flag hadn't been fluttering, I'd definitely have driven right past it. But shops like this, rooted in the local community, are surprisingly often delicious ✨ Still, the entrance inside the shop is so distinctive that you can't find it unless you're a local customer 😆
The entrance inside the shop
Inside the shop
Once inside, a more substantial menu than I expected was ready, and it has a great variety too 😋
Menu
Menu

Starting with the "Mix Soba" labeled as the No. 1 favorite, the lineup is quite varied, with soft-bone pork rib soba (nankotsu soki soba), braised pork belly soba (sanmai-niku soba), mazesoba, fu-suba with sea lettuce (āsa), black soba, and more. Prices are reasonable at ¥750 to ¥950, and the fact that you can also take out jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) is a nice point! This time I decided to order the No. 1 favorite "Mix Soba" (¥900) recommended by the staff member. Being able to enjoy both braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs is a real luxury, isn't it? 🤤

The shop isn't very large, but the homey, warm atmosphere is really nice 😊 Wooden tables and chairs are arranged, giving a nostalgic feeling like an old Okinawan diner. Various decorations and masks are displayed on the walls, so it's fun just to look around. The paper lanterns hanging from the ceiling add a nice touch too, and there was an atmosphere that reminded me of a festival stall. An electric fan spins round and round, a scene that's so very Okinawan, isn't it?
Mix Soba  ¥900

After ordering and waiting a while, the "Mix Soba" finally appeared! 😆 First, the visual impact is amazing. Chunks of braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs are piled in, and the fish cake and green onions are generously topped as well. The pink fish cake adds color, and it looks delicious just to look at ✨ The soup has a gentle, translucent color, and the lovely aroma of the blended broth rises up. My expectations are rising!
Let's start with a sip of the soup 😋 Yes yes, this is a blended broth with a solid pork-bone flavor! It's ordinarily tasty. It gently soaked into my body, tired from the end of the year 😌
Mix Soba  ¥900

Next, I try the noodles. These are medium-thick straight noodles, boiled to a soft texture 👍 People who like firmer noodles might find them a little lacking. The flavor of the noodles themselves is simple and doesn't get in the way of the soup's taste.

And now, the long-awaited toppings! First, the braised pork belly. Wow, this has been simmered until it's meltingly tender 😍 The seasoning is fairly sweet, with a gentle soy-sauce-based flavor. The soft-bone pork ribs are meltingly tender in the same way. These are also sweetly seasoned, finished with a gentle, Okinawan-style flavor.

Overall, my impression is of an ordinarily delicious Okinawa soba 😊 It doesn't have any particularly memorable features, but its steady deliciousness makes it easy to see why it continues to be loved by locals. As New Year's Eve soba, this gentle flavor may have been just right. It was a soba that gave me a warm, cozy feeling, as if healing a year's worth of fatigue ✨ My impression was that it was just ordinarily good.

Still, the distinctiveness of the entrance was memorable 😅 I'm sure first-time visitors will definitely get lost. But maybe that's part of Batten Soba's charm too. It feels like a hidden-gem shop that only locals know, which somehow makes you feel special. If you drive out toward Nanjo City, please stop by once. You can enjoy the ocean view too, and I think you can spend a relaxing time 🌊

Rating (9/15): Batten Soba was a shop that serves homey Okinawa soba that isn't flashy but that you can eat with peace of mind. The soup, noodles, and toppings were all of an ordinarily delicious quality, and it's understandable why it continues to be loved by locals 😊 The entrance is hard to find, but I think it's a shop you can enjoy including that. When you want to eat Okinawa soba in Sashiki Shinkai, Nanjo City, please remember Batten Soba!

高江洲そば.name: Takaesu Soba
高江洲そば.desc: An extremely popular shop that's sure to have a line, and the home of the "original yushi-dofu soba." A light, salty soup of pork bone, bonito, and kelp loaded with yushi-dofu (soft Okinawan tofu). You write your name on the whiteboard at the entrance and wait.
t: I ate here in September 2023, at this shop near the Pipeline Road 😁
The other day, on my way home from eating at "Suke Soba" along the same Pipeline Road (in Ginowan City), I found Takaesu Soba, so I decided "I'll go here next," and here I am lol
Takaesu Soba
Go a little way in from Pipeline Road and there's the shop, with a parking lot, but although it was lunchtime, it was amazingly full and I couldn't park (;^ω^)
And there are lots of customers lined up near the entrance!! I could tell it's a popular shop.
"This might be high-level Okinawa soba!" My expectations went up 🤗
I waited in the parking lot with my hazard lights on for a parking space to open up. After a while, customers who had finished eating left, and I finally got parked 😊
But now, waiting in line (;^ω^)
There was a bench outside with a few seats, and elderly people were sitting there, and I couldn't tell whether they were people resting outside after eating or people waiting their turn, so I asked.
It turned out there was a whiteboard at the entrance where you write your name. So I went to the entrance and wrote my name.
The whiteboard at the entrance. You write your name here and then wait to be called 😊
After waiting in line for quite a while, my turn finally came to go inside. You buy a ticket at the ticket machine set up near the entrance.
I came here without any research again, but the entrance said "original yushi-dofu soba," so I decided to order the yushi-dofu soba.
I decided on my order after seeing the "original yushi-dofu soba" at the entrance 😁
Yushi-dofu soba, large  ¥800
The toppings are green onions, egg, shredded pork spare ribs (soki), kūbu (knotted kelp), and yushi-dofu
The kelp reminded me of "Miyazato Soba" in Nago City lol
I ordered the "large," but the bowl seemed on the small side (medium size?)
On the ticket machine, the yushi-dofu soba came in "extra large," "large," and "medium," so even though it says "large," it might be the "medium" size at other shops.

First I tasted the soup 😊 It was like "Hm? What's the base?" and I couldn't really tell the flavor (;^ω^) Sorry for my dull palate (;^ω^) I thought it was very gentle and light. When I googled it, it's said to be a "light, salty soup using pork bone, bonito, and kelp," but since it also contains yushi-dofu, I could taste the flavor of the yushi-dofu liquid too.
The noodles are medium-thick, wavy, and on the soft side. Like the light soup, the other toppings were also lightly seasoned.

Rating (9/15): It's ordinarily tasty, but seeing the line of customers raised my expectations and I set the bar too high ^^; It seems to be a hugely popular shop, so why not try the original yushi-dofu soba?

鶏そば屋いしぐふー.name: Tori Soba-ya Ishigufu
鶏そば屋いしぐふー.desc: Provisional #4 (13.5/15). A popular shop in a renovated foreign-style house in Minatogawa. A clear salty soup of Yanbaru herb young chicken with in-house flat noodles, and two kinds of chicken chashu (salt chicken and seared chicken). A new style of Okinawa soba that's like salt ramen.
t: I ate here in December 2024 😄 This time I'm introducing "Tori Soba-ya Ishigufu," tucked into a corner of a residential area in Minatogawa, Urasoe City. It's a shop renovated from a building that was originally a foreign-style house, with an atmosphere that mixes nostalgia and stylishness. Even though it was a weekday, it was full of tourists and locals, and the wait was about the longest I've had, which shows how popular it is.
Tori Soba-ya Ishigufu (a shop renovated from a foreign-style house)
Tori Soba-ya Ishigufu. It's in a corner of Kansas Street
The menu is packed in all over the shop. From the standard chicken soba to creative, unusual variations, there's plenty to choose from 👇 (I'm introducing just part of the menu)

The No. 1 favorite, the "Special Chicken Soba." Two kinds of chicken, seared chicken and salt chicken, with in-house flat noodles and a broth made with Yanbaru herb young chicken, all with careful attention to detail
Chicken soba lineup (Special Chicken Soba, Chicken Salt Soba, Chicken Seared Soba, Green Onion-only Soba)
Vegetable soba  ¥1,000
Magic Special Black Mayu Oil Soba
Passionate Special Red Spicy Soba
Drink menu (including handmade ginger ale and floats too)
A view of the counter table

Now, what I ordered this time was the shop's top pick, the "Special Chicken Soba (medium)"! 🥢 In the bowl that was brought to me, in a clear chicken soup, shining in-house noodles, two kinds of chicken chashu (salt chicken and seared chicken), and vivid green onions were topped. Just from the look of it, it already feels like a winner ✨
Special Chicken Soba (medium)  ¥1,100

First, a sip of the soup... Mmm, it's delicious! 😋 This tastes more like a high-quality salt ramen than Okinawa soba. The broth made from Yanbaru herb young chicken has a perfectly balanced saltiness, and while it's refreshing, the umami of the chicken comes rushing in. I can't stop with my soup spoon with this soup 😆
Special Chicken Soba (medium)  ¥1,100

Next, the noodles. The in-house flat, wavy noodles are chewy and supple and pair superbly with the soup. Among the Ishigufu group, some shops finish the noodles a bit firm, but the noodles at the Minatogawa shop were just the right doneness. They have springiness while also being gentle on the palate, the type I'd recommend to anyone.

The salt chicken chashu topping is gently seasoned with a salty touch, moist and tender. A faint herb aroma gives it an elegant impression. The other one, the seared chicken, is fragrantly soaked in a sweet-and-salty soy sauce glaze, with a slightly punchy taste. Both had different personalities and were enjoyable, but personally I preferred the salt chicken 😊
Autographs of famous people displayed in the shop (could this be Robert's Baba-san, the gourmet who runs restaurants on Miyakojima?)
Autographs of famous people displayed in the shop
Autographs of famous people displayed in the shop (personal chopsticks are displayed too)

The interior has rows of autograph cards lined up, and you can tell many famous people visit. Anime and game pixel-art-style characters are also displayed on the walls, giving the shop a bit of a playful feel. The service was polite, and the atmosphere of the staff was warm.

However... the only drawback is "it gets so crowded!" The board inside the shop said "40+ minute wait," but I waited even longer 💦 Also, parking is limited, so if possible I recommend visiting on a weekday morning or at a time outside the peak.

Rating (13.5/15): Overall, I felt the Minatogawa shop is especially well-polished even among the Ishigufu shops. The balance of broth, noodles, and toppings was wonderful, and it was a bowl that proposes a new style of Okinawa soba. It's a shop I'd like to keep coming back to, and it's officially registered as a "Recommended Shop" ✨
